newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade surplus declines in November.
newsitem.headline: German trade surplus declines in November.

text.p: Germany's trade surplus declined slightly to 9.8 billion marks in November from 11.1 billion marks in October and 10 billion marks in November 1995, the Federal Statistics Office said.

The current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, showed a 200 million mark surplus in November, compared with a 1.3 billion mark deficit in October and a 600 million mark surplus in November 1995.

Exports in November were 70.6 billion marks, down from 74.9 billion the previous month but up from 67 billion a year earlier. Imports totalled 60.8 billion, compared with 63.8 billion and 57 billion, respectively.
Trade in services was in deficit by 4.0 billion marks, compared with shortfalls of 4.7 billion and 3.0 billion, respectively.

For the first 11 months of 1996, the trade surplus was 90.5 billion marks, up from 79 billion in the year-earlier period. The current account was in deficit by 23.5 billion marks versus 25.2 billion marks.

Exports totalled 718.5 billion marks, up from 686.1 billion marks, while imports were 628 billion, up from 607.1 billion marks. Trade in services was in deficit by 51.2 billion marks, compared with an identical shortfall in the year-earlier period. ($1 = 1.64 marks)
